source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
This standard practice document (aimed at agricultural extension agents and farmers) organizes corn production training into three stages: Stage 1 covers site selection, land preparation, seed/variety selection, pre-plant weed management, planting technique, and basal fertilizer; Stage 2 covers weed control and herbicides, plant nutrition, and topdressing; Stage 3 covers harvesting, drying, and storage.

Key cross-cutting recommendations highlighted in the document's summary section:

Corn requires a high level of soil fertility, especially nitrogen, so farmers should not plant corn in the same field continuously for many years in a row without addressing soil fertility.

Corn has weak tolerance to waterlogging, so it should never be planted on flood-prone/low-lying land.

Because the corn seed farmers currently plant is hybrid seed, farmers should not attempt to save seed from their harvest to replant in the following season, since hybrid offspring do not reliably retain the parent variety's characteristics.

The document also notes that two of the herbicides used for corn (referred to in the source as atrazine and 2,4-D) are true selective herbicides, but cautions that herbicides in general are not a guaranteed solution — using the wrong product, wrong timing, or wrong technique can fail to control weeds as intended, and pesticide use always carries a risk to human health if protective equipment is not used.

Overall, the document frames good land site selection, correct land preparation timing, quality seed, effective weed management timed to weed germination, correct planting spacing, and balanced basal and topdress fertilization (N, P, K) as the interconnected building blocks of high corn yield, followed by correctly timed harvest and adequate drying/storage to protect grain quality and value after harvest.
